scout.purpose: Real apps migrate incrementally, so Compose and Views need explicit ownership of lifecycle, state, themes, testing, and disposal at each boundary.
scout.realWorldUse: ComposeView embeds Compose in activities, fragments, or rows; AndroidView and AndroidViewBinding host existing Views inside a composable hierarchy.
scout.outcome: Choose the correct bridge direction, hoist shared state above it, and set disposal/update behaviour that matches the host lifecycle.

sections.title: ComposeView adds a composition to a View hierarchy

blocks.text: A ComposeView is a View whose content is produced by a Compose composition. It can replace one XML region while the activity or fragment remains View-based. Set a ViewCompositionStrategy that disposes composition according to the host: fragment content should normally follow the view-tree lifecycle so the composition does not retain a destroyed fragment view. Provide theme, state, and events from a shared state holder rather than keeping duplicate widget state on each side. Stable IDs matter when several ComposeViews participate in saved state.

blocks.caption: The composition lifetime follows the fragment view tree and receives state/events as ordinary inputs.

blocks.title: Compose in Views
rows: Compose theme aligned with host design system

View and Compose test surfaces as appropriate

sections.title: AndroidView hosts an existing View with create and update phases

blocks.text: AndroidView factory creates the View and should not be repeatedly recreated from changing state. The update block applies current Compose state whenever recomposition requires it. Avoid constructing the View outside factory with remember merely to work around ownership; use the API lifecycle. AndroidViewBinding inflates a binding and is convenient for complex existing XML or FragmentContainerView integrations. Listener callbacks should send events upward, while update renders the latest value without triggering feedback loops. Views with their own resource or cleanup lifecycle may need explicit release support.

blocks.caption: factory creates once for this node; update synchronises current state while avoiding needless text resets.

blocks.text: Choose a screen or leaf component with a clear state/event contract. Keep one source of truth above the boundary, then render it in either toolkit. Align colour, typography, spacing, accessibility, window insets, focus, and test tags/content descriptions. Avoid nesting toolkits repeatedly because debugging ownership and measurement becomes harder. Existing Views can remain where a mature library or custom widget has value; migration is not automatically deletion. Profile boundary-heavy lists and test configuration recreation, process restoration, dark mode, RTL, keyboard focus, accessibility, and screenshot differences before expanding the migration.

inspect.title: Find duplicate state ownership
inspect.code:
XML EditText stores body text
Compose preview stores remember { mutableStateOf(body) }
ViewModel stores body flow
Each listener updates a different copy
walkthrough: Three mutable owners can diverge after edits and recreation.
Interop is not the cause; duplicated state ownership is.
The ViewModel should own state while both renderers emit events and render current values.
inspect.expectedOutput: Hoist one state/event contract and remove toolkit-local domain copies.

trap_check.mistake: Keeping Compose and View copies of the same screen state.
trap_check.why: Updates and restoration diverge across the boundary.
trap_check.fix: Hoist one source of truth and pass state down/events up.

trap_check.mistake: Ignoring composition disposal in a fragment view.
trap_check.why: The composition may outlive and retain the destroyed view tree.

challenge_intro.task: Host an XML note editor inside a Compose screen with AndroidViewBinding, one ViewModel state source, correct listeners, dark/RTL/rotation tests, and no feedback loop.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Factory/inflation and update responsibilities are separate. Both toolkits render one shared immutable state. Lifecycle and restoration behaviour are verified.
